goals: Quantify how water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, subsurface drainage) responds to wet (1993) vs dry (2002) forcing across the watershed's spatial heterogeneity
Validate modeled runoff generation against USGS streamflow observations

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM can resolve soil moisture, ET, and runoff generation at points across the watershed. Comparing two forcing periods (1993 vs 2002) tests climate sensitivity. Spatial sampling captures heterogeneity in the response.

answerable: Wet-year (1993) vs dry-year (2002) contrast in partitioning (ET, runoff, drainage) at the watershed scale
How soil/topographic-position heterogeneity modulates the wet-vs-dry response
Analog validation of runoff generation timing and magnitude against USGS streamflow

not_answerable.aspect: Elevation's climate control on partitioning (orographic precip gradient, temperature lapse, rain-snow transition)
not_answerable.why: Framework provides uniform forcing to all columns; elevation-downscaled forcing (precip/temp lapse rates) is not implemented

not_answerable.aspect: Direct streamflow validation (routed hydrograph comparison at gauges)
not_answerable.why: ELM single-column produces column-scale runoff, not routed streamflow; framework lacks a routing model
not_answerable.needs: Runoff routing / aggregation to watershed outlet

sampling_strategy.approach: Stratified by elevation band and topographic position, with two forcing treatments (wet vs dry year)
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands × 2 topographic positions = 6 spatial strata. Light replication (2 columns per stratum) = 12 exploratory columns. Two forcing treatments (1993, 2002) × 12 = 24 exploratory columns. This resolves the wet-vs-dry contrast across the watershed's soil/position heterogeneity.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in valley/riparian zones (where soil moisture redistribution and runoff generation are strongest) and span the elevation gradient (which correlates with soil type and topographic wetness even without downscaled forcing). Upland columns capture drier, well-drained conditions; valley columns capture wetter, convergent zones.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 columns per spatial stratum to assess within-stratum variability and improve robustness of the wet-vs-dry contrast

sampling_plan.reason: Baseline partitioning in warm, low-elevation uplands under wet forcing
Contrast to wet year: how low-elevation uplands respond to drought
Runoff generation and soil moisture accumulation in convergent zones under wet forcing
Contrast to wet year: how valley zones sustain ET and runoff under drought
Intermediate elevation uplands under wet forcing (transition zone)
Contrast to wet year: mid-elevation upland drought response
Mid-elevation convergent zones under wet forcing (key runoff generation)
Contrast to wet year: mid-elevation valley drought response
High-elevation uplands under wet forcing (cooler, potentially snow-affected)
Contrast to wet year: high-elevation upland drought response
High-elevation convergent zones under wet forcing (headwater runoff generation)
Contrast to wet year: high-elevation valley drought response

sampling_plan.group: validation near USGS gauges, wet year (1993)
sampling_plan.reason: Analog validation of runoff generation timing/magnitude against observed streamflow in wet year

sampling_plan.group: validation near USGS gauges, dry year (2002)
sampling_plan.reason: Analog validation of runoff generation timing/magnitude against observed streamflow in dry year

validation_design.comparison: analog — modeled column-scale runoff (QOVER + QDRAI) compared to observed streamflow timing and wet-vs-dry ratio, NOT direct hydrograph matching (no routing)
validation_design.metric: Temporal correlation of monthly runoff generation vs observed streamflow; wet-year / dry-year runoff ratio
validation_design.n_validation_points: 2 (one per forcing treatment, near gauge locations)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: Two forcing periods (1993 wet, 2002 dry) applied to spatially stratified columns; native soil and vegetation per location

requires_capabilities.capability: Elevation-downscaled forcing (precipitation lapse rate, temperature lapse rate)
requires_capabilities.why: To isolate elevation's climate control on partitioning (orographic precip, rain-snow transition). Without it, elevation stratification tests soil/position heterogeneity, not climate gradient.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Answering whether elevation drives partitioning differences via climate (precip/temp gradients)

requires_capabilities.capability: Runoff routing / aggregation to watershed outlet
requires_capabilities.why: ELM produces column-scale runoff; USGS gauges measure routed streamflow. Direct hydrograph validation requires routing.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Direct streamflow validation (co-located hydrograph comparison at gauges)

requires_capabilities.why: Expander must sample real elevation data to place columns in specified elevation bands (900-1500m, 1500-2400m, 2400-3300m).
requires_capabilities.blocks: Automated placement of columns in elevation strata

requires_capabilities.capability: Gridded soil data (texture, depth, hydraulic properties)
requires_capabilities.why: To assign realistic soil properties by location, which control infiltration, runoff, and drainage.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Realistic soil heterogeneity in the sampling

requires_capabilities.capability: Topographic wetness index or valley-bottom mask
requires_capabilities.why: To identify valley/riparian vs upland positions for stratified sampling.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Automated placement of columns in topographic-position strata

requires_capabilities.why: To constrain sampling to the Salt River headwaters watershed.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Ensuring all columns are within the target domain

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS gauge metadata ingest (locations, drainage areas)
requires_capabilities.why: To place validation columns near gauges and retrieve observed streamflow for comparison.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Automated validation-column placement and observation retrieval

assumptions: 1993 and 2002 forcing data are available and representative of wet vs dry conditions in the Salt River headwaters
Uniform forcing (no elevation downscaling) is acceptable for a first-order wet-vs-dry contrast, with elevation stratification capturing soil/position heterogeneity rather than climate gradient
Analog validation (column runoff vs gauge streamflow) is scientifically defensible for assessing runoff generation timing and magnitude, despite lack of routing
USGS gauge locations are known and accessible for validation-column placement
Soil and vegetation data are available at sufficient resolution to assign realistic properties to sampled columns
SNOTEL sparsity is acceptable (snow processes are secondary to the wet-vs-dry partitioning question, though high-elevation columns may be affected)
open_questions: Are 1993 and 2002 confirmed as wet and dry years in this watershed (e.g. via precipitation anomaly or streamflow records)?
How many USGS gauges are active in HUC 15060103 during 1993 and 2002, and where are they located?
Is there interest in a follow-on experiment with elevation-downscaled forcing to isolate climate-gradient effects?
Should high-elevation columns include snow-related output variables (SWE, snowmelt timing) even though SNOTEL is sparse?
Is there interest in a coupled ELM-PFLOTRAN experiment to test groundwater's role in sustaining baseflow during the dry year?
